problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the subspace $S=\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the distance between $x$ and the subspace $S$ given that the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ is orthogonal.
worked_solution:
Since the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}{{a}_{1}}$ and $\text{Span}{{a}_{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{1}}{{a}_{1}\cdot {a}_{1}}{a}_{1}=\frac{0\cdot 4+1\cdot (-1)+1\cdot 1}{{4}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{1}^{2}}{a}_{1}=(0)[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{2}}{{a}_{2}\cdot {a}_{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{0\cdot 1+1\cdot 2+1\cdot (-2)}{{1}^{2}+{2}^{2}+(-2)^{2}}{a}_{1}=(0)[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=\overset{^}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the distance between $x$ and the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}d(x,\overset{^}{x}) & =‖x-\overset{^}{x}‖ \\  & =\sqrt{({x}_{1}-{\overset{^}{x}}_{1})^{2}+({x}_{2}-{\overset{^}{x}}_{2})^{2}+({x}_{3}-{\overset{^}{x}}_{3})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(0-0)^{2}+(1-0)^{2}+(1-0)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Note:** The fact that we got the zero-vector as the projection means that $x$ is orthogonal to the subspace $S.$
